sentences.text:
3. Heard Sri B.Harisughand Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner, as well as Sri S.Sudarshan,
learned Additional Public Prosecutor, representing the respondent-State.
4.

The prosecution case in brief is that the petitioner as Sub-Post Master has temporarily misappropriated Rs.2,52,30,000/- and permanently misappropriated Rs.2,42,819/- in SSP/NREGS/ Withdrawals/PLI/RPLI Deposits.

Thus, the petitioner has committed offences punishable under Sections 409, 420 of I.P.C.
5.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is innocent and the discrepancy is only on the ground of technical errors 2 NTR,J and even as per the complaint, the amount of Rs.2,52,30,000/- has been recovered and the other amount shown is only discrepancy between manual entries and the accounting in computing.
Further, the petitioner has no criminal antecedents so far in his office.
The petitioner is ready to co-operate with the judicial process and abide by any conditions that may be imposed.

However, as the petitioner is apprehending arrest,
prayed for grant of bail.

6. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor opposed bail application and submits that the petitioner is the responsible officer and he had temporarily misappropriated the funds of more than two and half crores for his personal benefits.
However, on findings in the Office, the petitioner has deposited those amounts excluding Rs.2,42,819/-.
Further, the petitioner is absconding from judicial process.
Thus, prayed for dismissal of the petition.
7. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel and the material placed on record.

sentences.text: The specific case of the prosecution is that the petitioner as Sub-Post Master has misappropriated the funds, which were given NREGS and there are specific overt acts substantiating the accusations in the complaint given by the Assistant Superintendent of Post Officer.
Having regard to these submissions, this Court is of the 3 NTR,J opinion that anticipatory bail cannot be granted in a case of this nature.

However, there is no reason as to why the petitioner should not surrender before the Investigating Officer for interrogation and then getting regular bail application disposed of by the Court concerned.

In the peculiar facts and circumstances, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the petitioner to surrender before the Investigating Officer on or before 21.06.2024 for the purpose of enquiry/interrogation and for recovery of incriminating materials if any.

After enquiry the petitioner shall be produced before the Court concerned having jurisdiction on the same day and the Court shall consider and dispose of the application, if any, filed by the petitioner for grant of regular bail, preferably on the same day on which day it is filed.
9. With the above directions, this Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, in this Criminal Petition shall stand closed.
